title: Climate Scientists Introduce Five Shared Socioeconomic Pathway Scenarios
content:
A decade ago, climate scientists introduced the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), a set of five scenarios designed to explore future socioeconomic development. The SSPs were created to help model how societies might evolve under varying conditions of climate adaptation and mitigation.

Each scenario outlines a distinct pathway for socioeconomic progress, taking into account different levels of challenge to climate adaptation and mitigation efforts. The framework allows researchers to assess how these divergent paths could influence climate outcomes and public health impacts.
summary: About a decade ago, a group of climate scientists described five scenarios for the future. These scenarios, called the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), suggest how socioeconomic development could evolve in worlds with differing challenges to climate adaptation and mitigation.
author: Phys.org

title: Physicists explain direction-dependent dielectric response in confined water
content:
Mehdi Neek-Amal and Francois Peeters at the University of Antwerp have identified the origins of a direction-dependent effect in water confined to a narrow gap between two plates. The physicists used an advanced mathematical model to analyze how this confined water responds to electric fields.

Their research, published in Physical Review Letters, demonstrates that two drastically different dielectric responses emerge from the natural bonding behavior of water molecules.
summary: Researchers at the University of Antwerp used a new mathematical model to reveal the origins of an unusual direction-dependent effect in water confined between two plates. Their study in Physical Review Letters showed that two different dielectric responses arise from the natural bonding behavior of water molecules.
author: Phys.org

title: AI surveillance at work provides minute‑by‑minute activity and productivity reports
content:
Artificial intelligence is transforming workplace surveillance by processing vast amounts of data to generate minute-by-minute accounts of employee activity and productivity. This evolution builds on historical monitoring methods, which have progressed from simple output targets to computer software commonly referred to as “bossware.”

UK technology editor Robert Booth discusses the current landscape of AI surveillance in an interview with Ian Sample. Booth details which sectors are adopting these advanced monitoring systems and the reasons behind their implementation. He also addresses the potential for these technologies to be counterproductive for employers.
summary: Workers have always been monitored by bosses through output targets and software called bossware, but AI now processes huge volumes of data to give minute‑by‑minute accounts of activity and productivity. UK technology editor Robert Booth explains which sectors are adopting this approach, why they are doing it, and how it could be counterproductive.
author: Guardian Science

title: Ito: A New Lua Library for Building Terminal User Interfaces
content:
Two developers have released Ito, a terminal user interface (TUI) library written in Lua, alongside a companion harness named Uji. The creators, who describe themselves as "Neovim nerds," chose Lua over JavaScript to allow for a minimal core design where every built-in abstraction and provider definition can be handled in Lua. The project is also capable of being based in Rust to improve performance.

To demonstrate the library's capabilities, one of the developers created a custom canvas implementation of Ito, which was exported as WebAssembly to power an interactive website for experimenting with Lua-based UIs. The team also included an "llms.txt" file to support AI-assisted coding. The Ito library is available at github.com/uji-labs/ito, and the Uji harness is hosted at github.com/uji-labs/uji.
summary: Developers have released Ito, a library that allows users to build terminal user interfaces entirely in Lua. The project includes a custom canvas implementation that runs in the browser via WebAssembly for interactive experimentation.
author: Hacker News

title: Aidlc: Adaptive workflow steering rules for AI coding agents
content:
AWS Labs has released "aidlc-workflows," a project designed to provide adaptive workflow steering rules for AI coding agents. The initiative is hosted on GitHub and has generated discussion on the Hacker News platform.

The project has garnered 15 points and 14 comments from the Hacker News community, reflecting early interest in its approach to managing AI-driven coding workflows.
summary: Aidlc introduces adaptive workflow steering rules for AI coding agents. The project is available on GitHub and has been discussed on Hacker News with 15 points and 14 comments.

content:
Show HN: Unfenced – Land for sale that borders public land

title: Pig kidneys rewarmed from -150°C freeze, work again for first time
content:
Scientists have successfully rewarmed pig kidneys that were cooled to -150 °C and stored in a freezer for months, demonstrating that the organs can function again. This achievement marks the first time such a process has been successfully completed, with the kidneys maintained in a glass-like state during storage.

The researchers hope to apply these findings to human organs in the future. The pig kidneys used in the study are similar in size to human kidneys.
summary: Scientists rewarmed pig kidneys that had been cooled to -150 °C and stored for months, and the organs worked again for the first time. The kidneys, similar in size to human ones, were left in a glass‑like state, and the researchers hope to replicate the findings with human organs.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind
content: The human sense of self-awareness is deeply connected to the brain, a three-pound organ containing billions of neurons and trillions of delicate connections. While science confirms the brain's role in defining individual identity, experts note that it remains difficult to fully explain the mechanisms behind self-awareness or pinpoint its exact location within the organ.
summary: The article discusses the role of the brain in identity and self‑awareness. It notes that while science links identity to the brain's structure, explaining self‑awareness remains challenging.

title: How much more can nuclear power plants give?
content:
Constellation, the largest nuclear operator in the United States, has announced plans to increase power output from its facilities. This move comes amid rising electricity demand, which has prompted efforts to maximize the capacity of existing power plants.

The announcement is part of a broader trend over the past few weeks, with nuclear power plants seeking to generate additional electricity to meet current market needs.
summary: In this age of rising electricity demand, people are trying to squeeze every last bit of power out of every power plant possible. Over the past few weeks, there’s been big news about nuclear power plants trying to do just that.

title: Zero-Click Spyware Infects Phones via Targeted Ads, Citizen Lab Releases Evidence
content:
‘Nightmare Scenario’: Zero‑Click Spyware Is Infecting Phones via Targeted Ads

Researchers at The Citizen Lab have for the first time released technical evidence that sophisticated mercenary spyware is being distributed through online advertising. The evidence shows the spyware can infect mobile phones without requiring any user interaction, using targeted ads as the delivery mechanism.
summary: Researchers at The Citizen Lab released technical evidence that sophisticated mercenary spyware is being distributed via online advertising. The spyware, described as zero-click, infects phones via targeted ads.

content: Democrats are preparing to investigate the Trump administration, but officials warn the effort may prove difficult. A recent government report on DOGE indicates that even obtaining basic information from the former administration will put a new Congress to the test.

title: Big Walk skips Xbox release to support BDS boycott of Microsoft
content:
Big Walk, a co‑op multiplayer walking adventure that launched in August, has become popular among players but has excluded Xbox users. The game's creators have now explained the reason for the exclusion.

Developer House House announced in a blog post that it chose not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles to align with the Palestinian‑led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement. The BDS movement calls for a boycott of Microsoft, including products under its gaming division.

Microsoft was named a priority BDS target in June last year because of contracts it has with the Israeli military and government, with the boycott specifically calling out Xbox consoles.
summary: Developer House House has decided not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles. The decision follows the Palestinian‑led BDS movement's call to boycott Microsoft, which includes Xbox products.
author: The Verge

title: Eiliko robot pet stores user data on Chinese servers, raising hack risk
content:
A new digital pet, a marshmallow‑shaped robot named Eiliko, has been sold on Amazon and marketed as a mood‑matching companion. According to a Verge article, the toy can change its cartoon expressions to reflect a user’s emotions and is designed for use over Wi‑Fi.

However, the Verge report warns that when the device is connected to the internet, it “phones home to China.” The AI companion can store everything a user says on Chinese servers, where the Verge notes that hackers could potentially gain access or hijack the device’s personality. The company that produces Eiliko, Energize Lab, is described in the article as appearing unconcerned about these security risks.

The author of the Verge piece purchased an Eiliko on August 29 and engaged in a 10‑minute conversation the following day. During that dialogue, the user asked the robot, “Do you ever tell anybody else what I’m saying?” and the toy replied, “Your secrets are safe with me.” The article concludes with a link to read the full story on The Verge.
summary: The Eiliko digital pet, made by Energize Lab, records conversations and saves them on servers in China. The Verge reports the data could be accessed or hijacked by hackers, and the company shows little concern.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon launches updated Bee Frontier and new Bee Eclipse wearable
content:
Amazon has expanded its Bee line of always‑listening AI wearables. The company acquired the startup last year and is now launching two new devices along with a subscription service.

The first product, the Bee Frontier, is priced at $74.99 and is an updated version of the original $50 Bee wearable. The second, the Bee Eclipse, will retail for $99.99 and is a credit‑card‑shaped gadget that snaps magnetically onto the back of a smartphone.

Both devices are marketed as tools to help users stay present. They record daily conversations and then generate summaries, transcripts, insights, and to‑do lists based on what they hear. Amazon is pairing the devices with a new subscription offering.
summary: Amazon announced two new Bee devices, the $74.99 Bee Frontier and the $99.99 Bee Eclipse. Both devices record conversations and provide summaries, transcripts, insights, and to‑dos.
author: The Verge

title: Ledger Launches Android-Based Atom Hardware Wallet Amid Southeast Asia Sales Halt
content:
Ledger has unveiled its newest crypto‑centric hardware effort, the Android‑based Atom. The device looks like a regular smartphone but is intended to be used alongside a phone rather than replace it.

The launch comes amid a challenging period for Ledger, which has had to stop selling some of its hardware in southeast Asia after a supply‑chain tampering incident that reportedly resulted in more than $86 million worth of cryptocurrency being stolen from users' accounts. Unlike Ledger’s earlier compact wallets that run custom software and often feature E Ink displays, the Atom is the spitting image of a standard Android smartphone.
summary: Ledger has announced its latest crypto‑centric hardware effort, the Android-based Atom, a device that resembles a phone but is instead designed to be used alongside one. It arrives at a tricky time for Ledger, which has been forced to cease sales of some of its hardware across southeast Asia following hardware tampering in its supply chain, which has reportedly seen over $86 million worth of crypto stolen from across some users' accounts.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon-owned Bee launches two new personal AI devices starting at $74.99
content:
Amazon‑owned Bee has introduced its first new AI devices since being acquired, launching an updated wearable and a credit‑card‑sized recorder that attaches to smartphones.  

The devices can summarize conversations, create to‑do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping. Prices for the new products start at $74.99.
summary: Amazon-owned Bee has released its first new AI devices since its acquisition, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches to smartphones. The devices can summarize conversations, create to-do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping, with prices starting at $74.99.

content:
Tech market sell‑off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt

The tech market sell‑off deepens amid fears over rising inflation and potential interest rate hikes. Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunged as the prospect of higher rates spooked markets.

An accelerating sell‑off of AI‑linked shares has hit global markets, with traders wary of the heavily indebted sector. The South Korea benchmark Kospi 200 index, heavily weighted toward memory‑chip companies, fell more than 8% overnight to a six‑month closing low, triggering circuit breakers that brought trading to a
summary: Chip makers and tech investors including Samsung and SoftBank fell sharply as worries over potential interest rate hikes spooked markets. South Korea’s Kospi 200 index dropped over 8% to a six‑month low, triggering circuit breakers and halting trading at times.

title: OpenAI sues former employee for leaking unreleased Apple product files
content:
OpenAI has filed a new claim in a lawsuit against Apple, alleging that a former employee who moved from the ChatGPT maker to the tech giant leaked confidential plans for an unreleased device. The filing, submitted in U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, states that the employee sent more than 100 files about the product to a personal account and later delivered a presentation on the same unreleased device to senior Apple leadership.

According to the lawsuit, the presentation took place months before the current legal dispute and Apple is now developing its own AI products, citing the recent release of Apple’s HomeView product. The claim adds a new layer of tension to the ongoing court proceedings between the two companies.
summary: OpenAI filed a lawsuit in US federal court in San Jose claiming a former employee who moved to Apple transferred over 100 files about an unreleased product to a personal account. The filing says the employee later presented the unreleased product to senior Apple leadership and notes Apple’s recent HomeView release as evidence of its AI work.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI surveillance at work expands, causing stress for teachers at Euan Blair firm
content:
A new podcast titled “Is your boss watching you? The rise of AI surveillance at work” examines how artificial‑intelligence tools are expanding workplace monitoring. Historically, workers have been overseen through output targets and software dubbed “bossware,” but AI now processes massive data streams to generate minute‑by‑minute accounts of employee activity and productivity.

In the episode, Guardian journalist Ian Sample speaks with UK technology editor Robert Booth, who outlines the sectors adopting AI‑driven surveillance, the motivations behind its use, and the risk that such monitoring could become counterproductive. Booth also highlights reports from teachers at Euan Blair’s firm, who say the AI system used to rate their work has caused “horrendous stress.”
summary: Workers have long been monitored, and AI is now enhancing “bossware” to generate minute‑by‑minute activity and productivity data. In the podcast, Ian Sample speaks with UK technology editor Robert Booth about sectors adopting the technology, its motivations and possible counterproductivity, noting teachers at Euan Blair’s firm report ‘horrendous stress’ after AI rated their work.
author: Guardian Technology

title: OpenAI London staff earned average £2.3m each in salary and shares last year
content:
OpenAI’s London operation paid its employees an average of £2,318,181 each in the most recent year, according to the company’s accounts. The Westminster‑based subsidiary, OpenAI UK Ltd, reported that 110 staff shared £87 million in salaries and £168 million in share awards.

The firm, which is behind the ChatGPT product, is establishing a new headquarters in London’s King’s Cross district while continuing to operate from its Westminster office. OpenAI UK Ltd is preparing for a potential stock‑market listing at a valuation of roughly $1 trillion.
summary: Accounts for OpenAI UK Ltd show that 110 employees shared £87 million in salaries and £168 million in shares last year. The average compensation per staff member was £2,318,181.
author: Guardian Technology

title: At least two dead as heavy rain and flooding shut down Istanbul
content:
At least two people were killed after heavy rain and widespread flooding forced a shutdown of Istanbul, officials said.  

The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality reported that some parts of the city experienced the highest amount of rain since 1985.  

The severe weather prompted authorities to halt activities across the metropolis as emergency measures were implemented.
summary: At least two people were killed after heavy rain and widespread flooding shut down Istanbul. The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality said some areas received the highest rainfall since 1985.

content: A midday news bulletin released on October 15, 2026 offered a roundup of the most important stories from Europe and beyond. The bulletin highlighted the latest and breaking news across a range of topics, including world affairs, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.

title: FSB arrests Swedish citizen in Pskov on terrorism charges amid talk of prisoner swaps
content:
Moscow’s Federal Security Service (FSB) detained a Swedish citizen in the Pskov region on terrorism charges, while Japanese journalist Yuki Imai was arrested on Sakhalin on espionage charges. The arrests come days after former president Dmitry Medvedev wrote that Russia may need to “fill up the exchange pool with European and American idiots” to secure the release of Russians held abroad.

The timing of the detentions suggests Moscow is positioning the two foreign nationals for potential future prisoner swaps, according to the context of Medvedev’s comments. No further details on the individuals’ identities or the specific allegations were provided.
summary: The FSB arrested a Swedish citizen in Russia's Pskov region on terrorism charges and journalist Yuki Imai on Sakhalin on espionage charges. The arrests came days after former president Medvedev wrote that Russia may need to “fill up the exchange pool with European and American idiots” to recover Russians abroad.

title: Israel and Iran hold rare confidence‑building summit in Baku, Azerbaijan says hub
content:
Israel and Iran met in Baku for a rare “confidence‑building measures” summit, an event described by Azerbaijan as a connecting hub in the Eurasian space.  

The summit brought together the two Middle‑East rivals in Azerbaijan’s capital, marking an uncommon diplomatic engagement between the in‑conflict parties. Azerbaijan highlighted the meeting as evidence of its role as a regional bridge.  

Azerbaijan’s officials said the gathering underscores Baku’s position as a hub linking Eurasian nations.
summary: Israel and Iran met in Baku for a rare “confidence‑building measures” summit. Azerbaijan said the meeting shows the city is a connecting hub in the Eurasian space.
author: Euronews

title: Oxfam France launches legal challenge alleging tax reforms favor wealthy
content:
Paris – French poverty has reached its highest level in decades and hunger is on the rise, according to a headline highlighting the impact of President Emmanuel Macron’s economic policies.  

Oxfam France is contesting the state’s tax system on constitutional grounds, saying that recent fiscal reforms have mainly benefited the wealthiest and deepened economic inequality. Director of Advocacy Nicolas Vercken told a gathering hosted by Charles Pellegrin that the issue is “not so much about how much the percentage of tax and the burden of our tax system, it’s who you tax and for what.”  

The organization has launched a legal initiative to determine whether the French government has failed to meet its constitutional obligations, a move that could place fiscal inequality under judicial review for years.
summary: Nicolas Vercken, Director of Advocacy for Oxfam France, said the organization is challenging the French state's constitutional obligations over tax inequality, arguing that successive fiscal reforms have disproportionately benefited the wealthiest. The legal initiative seeks to place fiscal inequality under judicial scrutiny for years to come.
author: France 24

title: Companies rent sensor‑equipped spy planes worldwide for political missions
content:
Companies around the world are leasing aircraft equipped with advanced sensors to military and intelligence customers for political missions, according to a recent analysis of the global spy‑plane market. The rentals span locations from the Mexican border to Syria and the Sahel region.

The market operates with a low public profile, yet its activities are observable across these diverse theatres. The demand for sensor‑laden planes underscores the role of private providers in supporting armed forces and intelligence services worldwide.
summary: Companies are renting out planes equipped with powerful sensors to armies and intelligence services from the Mexican border to Syria and the Sahel. The spy plane market is discreet but not invisible.
author: France 24

title: China and North Korea open Yalu River Bridge linking Dandong and Sinuiju
content:
China and North Korea formally opened the Yalu River Bridge on Thursday, linking the Chinese city of Dandong with the North Korean city of Sinuiju.  

Beijing said the new crossing is intended to promote economic and trade cooperation between the two nations.  

The bridge now provides a direct connection across the Yalu River between Dandong and Sinuiju.
summary: China and North Korea formally opened the Yalu River Bridge on Thursday, connecting Dandong in China with Sinuiju in North Korea. Beijing says the bridge will promote economic and trade cooperation.
author: France 24

title: US Defense Secretary announces plan to livestream firing‑squad execution of Fort Hood shooter
content:
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced last week that the government intends to livestream the firing‑squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. The proposal has sparked a backlash from Republicans in Congress, religious leaders and international observers.

Death‑penalty experts note that a government execution has never been broadcast or livestreamed, and the U.S. military has not carried out a firing‑squad execution since 1945, making the plan an unprecedented move. France 24’s International Affairs commentator Douglas Herbert reported on the reaction.
summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced plans to livestream the firing‑squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. The proposal has drawn backlash from Republicans in Congress, religious leaders and international observers, and experts note no U.S. execution has ever been broadcast and the military has not used a firing squad since 1945.
author: France 24

title: Zelensky says Ukraine will ignore Trump's ban on Russian refinery strikes
content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Kyiv will no longer follow U.S. President Donald Trump’s request to refrain from striking Russian oil refineries. The statement, published on Thursday, comes as tensions rise between the two leaders over a U.S.–Russia diesel agreement.

Relations between Kyiv and Washington have deteriorated since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large quantities of diesel onto global markets. FRANCE 24 International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley reported on the growing dispute.
summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine will no longer abide by US President Donald Trump's demand not to strike Russian oil refineries. He made the remarks amid deepening tensions after Trump eased sanctions on Russia in a diesel agreement that released large amounts of diesel onto global markets.
author: France 24

title: Chad plans to withdraw from ICC, sparking worries about Sudan war crimes probes
content:
Chad announced in July that it intends to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, saying the court is inefficient and disproportionately targets African nations.  

The planned exit could hinder future ICC investigations into alleged war crimes linked to the conflict in neighbouring Sudan, as investigators are currently working with Sudanese refugees sheltering in eastern Chad.  

Humanitarian organisations continue to operate in the area, providing assistance to those displaced by the crisis, according to FRANCE 24’s Harold Girard.
summary: In July, Chad announced plans to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, accusing the court of inefficiency and of disproportionately targeting African nations. The move could complicate ICC investigations of alleged war crimes in the neighbouring Sudan conflict, as investigators work with Sudanese refugees in eastern Chad.
author: France 24

title: Starlink disruption in Ukraine amid US pressure and Musk's closer ties to Trump
content:
SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service was recently disrupted in Ukraine, a development that coincides with increased pressure from Washington on Kyiv to cease its strikes against Russian oil refineries.  

Starlink is identified as a key component of Ukraine’s long‑range drone operations, and the interruption of the service has prompted questions about the potential impact on those capabilities.  

The situation also highlights growing attention to Elon Musk’s increasingly close ties with Donald Trump, as observers consider how the relationship might influence the disruption and its broader implications for Ukraine.
summary: SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine was recently disrupted. The disruption occurs as Washington pressures Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries and comes amid Elon Musk’s increasingly close ties with Donald Trump.
author: France 24

title: North Korea and China open New Yalu River Bridge after 12-year delay
content:
The New Yalu River Bridge linking China and North Korea has entered service twelve years after its construction was completed. The border crossing is now operational, marking the first use of the bridge since it was built.

Officials described the opening as the latest indication of warming ties between the two neighboring nations.
summary: The New Yalu River Bridge between China and North Korea became operational twelve years after its construction. The opening is described as the latest sign of warming ties between the two nations.

content: Brazil is heading back to the polls, a move that could have implications beyond its borders. content:
Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing

Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace, and seven crew members are missing.
summary: Two chemical tankers caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

title: WHO calls for faster action to curb lead exposure killing 3.5 million annually
content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) called on governments on Thursday to speed up measures that prevent lead exposure.  

WHO said lead exposure is estimated to cause more than 3.5 million deaths worldwide each year and to affect hundreds of millions of children.  

The agency urged countries to accelerate their efforts to end the health impacts of lead.
summary: The World Health Organization said on Thursday that countries must accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure. WHO estimates lead exposure causes more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year and affects hundreds of millions of children.
author: UN News

title: Senegal detains over 320 LGBTQ+ individuals amid tightened anti-homosexuality law
content:
LGBTQ+ individuals in Senegal are increasingly going into hiding as a wave of arrests targets the community, according to a new Human Rights Watch (HRW) report.  

The report, citing the HIV Justice Network, says more than 320 people have been detained on accusations of “acts against nature” since February, following the recent tightening of Senegal’s law criminalising homosexuality. The crackdown includes mass arrests, forced HIV testing and obstacles to obtaining legal representation.  

Among those detained, at least 84 have been charged with “voluntary HIV transmission” on the sole basis of their HIV status. The HRW report documents these actions as part of an escalating campaign against LGBTQ+ people in the country.
summary: At least 320 people have been arrested in Senegal for alleged "acts against nature" since February, according to the Human Rights Watch report. The crackdown includes forced HIV testing and charges of voluntary HIV transmission, with 84 individuals charged solely because of their HIV status.
author: Guardian World

title: Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia may be delayed a year amid Houthi attacks
content:
The Asian Cup scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia may be postponed by a year amid Houthi attacks, according to the AFC president.  

The tournament is set to begin on January 7, but the AFC president said it could be moved by a year if necessary.
summary: The tournament scheduled to begin on Jan. 7 in Saudi Arabia could be postponed by a year. AFC president said the delay may be considered because of Houthi attacks.

title: FIFA to ban overturning of match suspensions after Balogun red‑card row
content:
FIFA is preparing a rule change following a red‑card controversy involving player Balogun at the World Cup, according to reports.  

The governing body’s council is expected to adopt a policy that would bar disciplinary committees from overturning match suspensions.  

If approved, the new rule would prevent future reversals of suspensions imposed during games.
summary: FIFA’s council is expected to prohibit disciplinary committees from overturning match suspensions. The change follows a red‑card dispute involving Balogun at the World Cup.

content:
Syrian authorities have arrested the main suspect in the 2013 Baniyas mass killings.  

The individual, identified as Ali Kayali and also known as Mihrac Ural, was apprehended while trying to cross the border, state media reported.  

The arrest was confirmed by the state‑run news outlet.
summary: Syrian authorities arrested Ali Kayali, also known as Mihrac Ural, as the main suspect in the 2013 Baniyas mass killings. He was apprehended while trying to cross the border, according to state media.

title: Shai Hope jokes about record role and excess baggage ahead of India series finale
content:
West Indies batsman Shai Hope said he was “worried about excess baggage” after receiving the latest Player of the Match award in the thrilling India‑West Indies series.  

Hope’s comment came as the bilateral series approached its final match, with the contest described as exciting.  

The remark highlighted Hope’s light‑hearted view of his role as the series draws to a close.
summary: Shai Hope joked that his record role in the India‑West Indies series could become a problem as the series finale looms. He said he was worried about excess baggage after earning his latest Player of the Match award in the thrilling series.

title: Obama says drift towards extremism not inevitable as 12,000 attend city venue
content:
Former US President Barack Obama said that a drift toward extremism “is not inevitable,” emphasizing his view that the world can avoid such a trajectory.  

More than 12,000 people filled a major venue in the city to hear Obama’s remarks on the challenges the world is facing.
summary: Obama said the drift towards extremism is not inevitable. More than 12,000 people filled a major venue in the city to hear the former US president's take on the challenges the world is facing.

title: Brazil Congress approves shorter working week, seen as win for Lula
content:
Brazil’s Congress approved a measure to shorten the working week, a development described as a win for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.  

Supporters of Lula said the legislation could increase his popularity as the country heads toward a presidential run‑off scheduled in ten days.
summary: Brazil's Congress approved a shorter working week. Lula's supporters hope the measure will boost his popularity ahead of a presidential run‑off in 10 days.

title: Russia accuses Ukraine of oil refinery attack as Zelensky says strikes will resume
content:
Russia has charged Ukraine with carrying out an attack on an oil refinery, a claim that follows Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s announcement that a pause on striking energy sites is ending.

Zelensky said the suspension of attacks on Russian energy infrastructure would be lifted after fresh Russian attacks, signaling a resumption of strikes against such targets.
summary: Russia alleges that Ukraine attacked an oil refinery. Ukraine's president Zelensky says the pause on striking energy sites is over after fresh Russian attacks.
author: BBC World

title: SpaceX delivers over 6,000 pounds of cargo to ISS with CRS-35 Dragon
content:
SpaceX’s CRS‑35 cargo Dragon is scheduled to rendezvous with the International Space Station today, October 15, after a two‑day chase. The spacecraft will deliver more than 6,000 pounds of cargo to the orbiting laboratory.

The launch and docking will be available for live viewing.
summary: SpaceX's CRS-35 cargo Dragon will rendezvous with the International Space Station today (Oct. 15) after a two-day chase. The launch will be broadcast live for viewers to watch.
author: Space.com

title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
content:
Lisandro Martínez has publicly criticized Manchester United’s ownership, arguing that the club’s problems stem from deeper issues than individual player mistakes. In a recent appearance on Amazon Prime, Martínez said the team’s “indifferent start to the season” is partly due to his own high‑profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham.

The defender’s remarks came after United’s 2‑0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night. Martínez appeared in a hot‑dog costume and mocked innocence while discussing the loss, suggesting that the club’s struggles go beyond on‑field performance.

Former United players reacted to Martínez’s comments. Wayne Rooney called him “disrespectful,” Ashley Young said he “doesn’t feel like he’s got the right,” and Rio Ferdinand noted on his podcast that “These things don’t end well, man.”
summary: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the clubHeartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season, given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Papua New Guinea's Rugby League Brings Unity to 800-Language Nation Ahead of World Cup
content:
World Cup co‑hosts Papua New Guinea celebrate their love of rugby league through the national teams of the Kumuls and the Orchids. The sport’s popularity is evident in the pride and unity these teams inspire across the island.

The Kumuls and Orchids serve as badges of hope and unity for Papua New Guinea, a nation of 800 languages, during the upcoming World Cup.
summary: Papua New Guinea, a World Cup co-host, is known for its love of rugby league. The Kumuls and the Orchids national teams are badges of hope and unity for the island's 800 languages.
author: BBC Sport

title: European figures urge Arsene Wenger to challenge Infantino for Fifa presidency
content:
Senior figures in European football have expressed a desire for former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to enter the race for the Fifa presidency. According to BBC Sport, these influential individuals view Wenger as a potential surprise candidate who could challenge the current incumbent, Gianni Infantino.

The proposal suggests a significant shift in the leadership dynamics of world football, positioning Wenger as a direct contender against Infantino.
summary: Senior figures in European football have told BBC Sport that they want former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to run as a surprise candidate. They specifically want him to run against Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency.
author: BBC Sport

title: Cait Conley urges Rep. Mike Lawler not to mansplain domestic abuse
content: Democrat Cait Conley instructed Republican Rep. Mike Lawler not to “mansplain” to her about domestic abuse during a televised debate on Wednesday night. The exchange occurred as the candidates discussed an alleged gang rape that took place at a Cornell University fraternity in 2024. The debate was moderated by a representative from PIX11 News, an affiliate of Nexstar Media Group.
summary: Democrat Cait Conley told Rep. Mike Lawler (R-N. Y.) during a televised debate on Wednesday night not to mansplain her about domestic abuse. The debate covered an alleged gang rape at a Cornell University fraternity in 2024.

title: James Talarico Holds CNN‑Jubilee Town Hall to Urge Ken Paxton Debate
content:
Texas Democrat James Talarico held a town hall on Wednesday, taking questions from voters in a session hosted by CNN and Jubilee. The event featured Talarico on stage alone as he urged his Republican rival, Gov. Ken Paxton, to join him in a debate amid the closely watched Senate race.

Talarico, a state lawmaker and Presbyterian seminarian, used the forum to emphasize unity, stating “we’re all on the same team.” He called for a direct debate with Paxton, arguing that such a discussion would benefit the electorate in the competitive Senate contest.
summary: Texas Democrat James Talarico, a state lawmaker and Presbyterian seminarian, took questions from voters during a town hall hosted by CNN and Jubilee on Wednesday. He urged rival Republican Ken Paxton to debate in their closely watched Senate race.
author: The Hill

title: Trump’s approval rating hits record low in Fox News poll
content: A new Fox News survey indicates that President Trump’s overall approval rating has reached a record low for either of his terms. The poll reflects growing voter dissatisfaction with his management of key issues, with 36 percent of respondents approving of his overall handling of the presidency. Conversely, 64 percent of respondents disapproved of his performance.
summary: A Fox News survey found President Trump’s overall approval rating at a record low, with 36% approval and 64% disapproval. The decline reflects growing voter dissatisfaction with his handling of key issues.
author: The Hill

title: Trump questions US negotiators' identity in Iran talks at Montana rally
content:
President Trump expressed uncertainty at a rally in Montana on Wednesday night about who U.S. officials were negotiating with in efforts to end the Iran war. “I don’t know who the hell we’re negotiating with,” he said.

He added that the group in question “don’t have a navy. They don’t have an air force. Their army is decimated. Their leaders are gone,” referencing the state of the Iranian military and leadership.
summary: President Trump stated at a Montana rally that he was unsure who U.S. officials were negotiating with to end the Iran war. He claimed Iran's military forces are decimated and its leaders are gone.
author: The Hill

title: NHS Diagnosis Gap: Fewer Than 1 in 15 South London Teens with Mental Disorders
content:
A new study from the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience (IoPPN) at King's College London estimates that fewer than one in 15 young people in south London who have a mental health disorder may have received a diagnosis from NHS mental health services.

The research highlights a gap between the prevalence of mental health disorders among south London teens and the proportion that are formally diagnosed by NHS services.
summary: A new study by the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at King's College London found that fewer than one in 15 young people in south London who have a mental health disorder may have received a diagnosis from NHS mental health services. The study highlights a significant gap in NHS diagnosis coverage for these teens.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Large MRI dataset reveals consistent adolescent brain wiring patterns
content:
Researchers have developed a large, openly available neuroimaging resource comprising more than 24,000 MRI scans from over 10,000 adolescents. This dataset offers insights into how the brain’s wiring develops during the adolescent years.

To compile the resource, the team utilized advanced, open-source image-processing methods. These techniques allowed them to identify highly consistent patterns of development across 21 distinct study sites, successfully accounting for variations in scanner technology and image quality.
summary: Researchers released an openly available neuroimaging resource that includes more than 24,000 MRI scans of over 10,000 adolescents, mapping brain wiring changes during adolescence. Advanced open-source image-processing methods revealed highly consistent developmental patterns across 21 study sites, despite variations in scanner technology and image quality.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Purdue scientist uses lasers and Doppler effect to personalize chemotherapy
content:
Purdue University scientist David Nolte is developing an imaging system that could tailor chemotherapy to individual tumors. The system uses laser light, the Doppler effect, and artificial intelligence to assess how a specific cancer responds to various drugs.

Nolte’s approach aims to provide early insight into tumor drug sensitivity, a step that could improve treatment outcomes as the number of available chemotherapy agents grows. By identifying the most effective drug for each patient’s unique cancer, the technology seeks to personalize therapy and reduce trial‑and‑error.

The project is still in development, but it represents a new direction in cancer treatment research that focuses on the individuality of each tumor.
summary: Purdue University scientist David Nolte is developing an imaging system that utilizes laser light, the Doppler effect, and AI. The technology aims to provide early insight into how individual tumors respond to specific chemotherapy drugs.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Parents of kids who need complex medical care at home tend to resolve frequent safety issues on their own, study finds
content:
A study published in the journal Pediatrics by researchers from Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago highlights the challenges faced by parents of medically complex children. Approximately one in 20 U.S. children under the age of 18 are considered medically complex, a classification that includes those with multiorgan system conditions such as cerebral palsy who rely on implanted tube-related medical technology.

These children receive the majority of their care at home, placing the responsibility on parents to manage complicated devices and intricate medication and nutrition regimens. The study found that while these parents frequently encounter safety challenges in this role, they typically develop creative solutions to address these issues without involving the child's care team.
summary: Approximately 1 in 20 U. S.
author: Medical Xpress

title: STING Pathway Identified as Potential Target to Treat Age-Related Bone Loss
content:
Researchers are exploring the STING signaling pathway as a possible target for treating bone loss that occurs with aging.  

Osteoporosis, the condition that makes bones weak and brittle, is driven by changes in the cells of the bone marrow microenvironment.  These changes include elevated fat and immune cells that promote inflammation.  

The STING pathway is known to drive inflammation, but its role in aging bones has until now been unclear.
summary: Osteoporosis, the age-related weakening of bones, is driven by changes in bone marrow cells, including increased fat and inflammation-promoting immune cells. The STING signaling pathway is a molecular driver of inflammation, but its role in aging bones has been unclear until recent research.
author: Medical Xpress

title: 143 of 154 Developing Countries Have National Adaptation Plans, Implementation Lagging
content:
Climate adaptation's delivery gap: Turning national plans into action

By 2025, 143 of 154 developing countries had established a National Adaptation Plan process. Despite this progress, implementation has not kept pace with the plans.

Many countries still lack the institutional capacity, project preparation, and finance needed to transform their priorities into actionable strategies, bankable projects, and tangible results on the ground.
summary: By 2025, 143 of 154 developing countries had a National Adaptation Plan process in place. However, many still lack the institutional capacity, project preparation, and finance needed to implement these plans into actionable projects and results.
author: Phys.org

title: Galapagos Marine Iguanas Face Survival Threat from Black‑Market Trafficking Amid Super El Niño
content:
Scientists warn that the Galapagos marine iguana, the only lizard capable of living and foraging at sea, may face a survival crisis.  

International researchers report that black‑market trafficking of these iguanas is peaking at the same time that a super El Niño event is decimating their natural food sources.
summary: International scientists warn that black‑market trafficking of Galapagos marine iguanas is peaking. The super El Niño is decimating their natural food source, threatening their survival.
author: Phys.org

title: CSIRO report finds growing options to cut on-farm emissions
content:
A new report by CSIRO, Australia’s national science agency, has identified investment priorities for low‑emissions agriculture.  

The report finds a growing suite of promising options already available to reduce on‑farm emissions.  

It also highlights further opportunities for practical solutions that Australian producers can adopt.
summary: CSIRO, Australia's national science agency, found a growing suite of promising options already available to reduce on-farm emissions. The report also identifies further opportunities for practical solutions for Australian producers.
author: Phys.org

title: EIT Food Observatory Report: Consumers Need Clear Answers on Precision Fermentation
content:
Consumers may not fully understand precision fermentation yet, but many are curious enough to taste the results, according to new qualitative research from the EIT Food Consumer Observatory. The study, published ahead of World Food Day on Oct. 16, indicates that this curiosity presents a significant opportunity for food innovation.

The research emphasizes that companies must answer consumers’ questions clearly and deliver a satisfying first bite to build trust. The findings highlight the importance of transparency and product quality in the growing precision fermentation market.
summary: Qualitative research from the EIT Food Consumer Observatory, published ahead of World Food Day on Oct. 16, shows consumers are curious about precision fermentation but lack clear understanding. The study suggests companies must answer questions clearly and deliver on the first bite to turn curiosity into an opportunity for food innovation.
author: Phys.org

title: Ascension Island's planting project creates lush cloud forest
content:
Ascension Island: How a planting project created a lush cloud forest

In the middle of nowhere, a small island emerges in the Atlantic Ocean. This unique territory completely changed in the 19th century thanks to the efforts of two British scientists: Charles Darwin and Joseph Dalton Hooker.  

Both researchers stopped at the British naval base and documented the island during their expeditions. Their observations marked a significant moment in the island’s history.
summary: A planting project on Ascension Island created a lush cloud forest. The island’s 19th‑century transformation was documented by British scientists Charles Darwin and Joseph Dalton Hooker during their visits to the British naval base.
author: Phys.org

title: Russia and China use AI to launch relentless cyberattacks on UK
content:
Russia and China are employing artificial intelligence to conduct relentless cyberattacks against the United Kingdom, according to recent reports.  

The use of AI is accelerating the speed of these attacks on UK infrastructure, making them more rapid and potentially more damaging.  

At the same time, AI technologies are also being deployed to help defend the United Kingdom’s critical systems against such threats.
summary: Russia and China are using artificial intelligence to stage relentless cyberattacks against the UK. AI is increasing the speed of attacks on UK infrastructure while also being used to help defend against them.
author: New Scientist

title: Whalefall Review: Gruesome Film About Diver Swallowed by Sperm Whale
content:
Whalefall review: Worth watching for the bits inside a sperm whale

The film Whalefall, adapted from Daniel Kraus’s novel, follows a diver who is swallowed by a sperm whale. Critics describe the movie as terrifically gruesome, with intense and graphic scenes that highlight the perilous nature of the story.

Bethan Ackerley, in her review, notes that while the film delivers on visceral horror, it also leans heavily into sentimentality, which she finds excessive. The review suggests that viewers seeking the raw, shocking moments of the whale’s interior may find the film worthwhile, though the emotional tone may not appeal to everyone.
summary: The film, based on Daniel Kraus’s novel, follows a diver swallowed by a sperm whale. Bethan Ackerley calls it terrifically gruesome but far too sentimental.
author: New Scientist

title: Professor Eric So Discusses AI's Impact on Thinking in New Book
content:
A new book by Professor Eric So examines how technology influences thinking skills, framing the discussion as a “collision” between artificial intelligence, the human brain, and society. The work is presented in a Q&A format that probes the ways AI interacts with cognition and social structures.

So’s analysis focuses on the impact of AI on mental processes, exploring how emerging tools reshape the way people think and learn. The book aims to illuminate the broader implications of this technological intersection for individuals and communities.
summary: Professor Eric So has published a new book that examines how AI technology affects thinking skills. The book explores the collision between AI, the brain, and society.
author: MIT News

title: Cancers Rising Faster in Younger English Adults, Scientists Seek New Causes
content:
A major study has identified that several cancers are increasing more rapidly among younger adults in England, even as traditional risk factors such as smoking, diet and other established contributors have generally improved.  

The analysis found that excess weight accounts for only a portion of the rise, prompting researchers to investigate additional explanations. Potential factors under consideration include alterations in the gut microbiome and exposures experienced early in life.  

Scientists acknowledge that the reasons for the accelerating cancer rates in younger populations remain incompletely understood.
summary: A major study found that several cancers are rising faster among younger adults in England, even as smoking, diet, and other established risk factors have generally improved. Excess weight explains only part of the increase, leaving scientists searching for other possible causes such as changes in the gut microbiome and early-life exposures.
author: Science Daily

title: 47-year study finds fitness and strength start declining around age 35
content:
A 47‑year longitudinal study has identified a key milestone in physical aging, finding that fitness and strength start to decline around age 35. The research shows that this downturn occurs even among individuals who maintain regular exercise routines.

The investigators observed that the rate of decline speeds up as people grow older, indicating an accelerating loss of physical capacity over time. Despite the early onset of this decline, the study notes that beginning an exercise regimen in adulthood can still enhance overall physical performance.

These findings suggest that while age‑related strength loss begins in the mid‑30s, targeted physical activity later in life remains beneficial for maintaining functional ability.
summary: A 47-year study found that fitness and strength begin declining around age 35, even among regular exercisers. Researchers said the decline accelerates as people get older, but starting to exercise in adulthood can still improve physical performance.
author: Science Daily

title: 120‑million‑year‑old fossil uncovers new European megaraptoran dinosaur
content:
A 120‑million‑year‑old fossil that had lain forgotten in a museum for nearly a century has been identified as a new, fearsome dinosaur.  

The tiger‑sized predator, noted for its giant claws, was described as potentially more dangerous to humans than a Tyrannosaurus rex. Its remains constitute the first evidence of megaraptorans in Europe, offering insight into how this group of mysterious dinosaurs later evolved into gigantic hunters.  

The find expands the known diversity of European dinosaurs from the mid‑Cretaceous period.
summary: A 120‑million‑year‑old fossil forgotten in a museum for nearly a century revealed a new dinosaur. The tiger‑sized predator provides the first evidence of megaraptorans in Europe and may have been more dangerous to humans than a T. Rex.
author: Science Daily

title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to slight risk of sudden vision loss
content:
Popular diabetes and weight‑loss medications Ozempic and Wegovy have been linked to a slightly increased risk of a rare condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss, according to recent research.

Rutgers researchers noted that while the risk remains very low, the findings merit attention because millions of people are using GLP‑1 medications such as these drugs.
summary: Rutgers researchers found that the diabetes and weight‑loss drugs Ozempic and Wegovy are linked to a slightly increased risk of a rare condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss. The risk is described as very low, but the researchers say the finding merits attention as millions use GLP‑1 medications.
author: Science Daily

title: Tropical fires spread to central and eastern Amazon during El Niño
content:
Fires have reached the central and eastern Amazon rainforest as part of a broader tropical blaze linked to the El Niño weather pattern.  

The cascade of fires began in equatorial Asia and then spread across the tropics, continuing into the Amazon region. The ongoing blazes are occurring during the current El Niño episode.
summary: During El Niño, a cascade of fires across the tropics began in equatorial Asia. The fires then continued in the central and eastern Amazon.

content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) posted on 15 October 2026 featured an image titled “The Milky Way over Manhattan.” The daily APOD entry showcases a photograph of the night sky with the Milky Way visible above the New York City skyline.

content:

title: Flipflop: iroh-powered persistent tunnels for file sharing announced on Hacker News
content:
A developer announced a new project titled “Flipflop, iroh‑powered persistent tunnels for filesharing” in a Show HN post. The tool was created after the author’s frustrations with using LocalSend and DashBeam to transfer files between devices.

Flipflop aims to provide fast file transfers, incorporates the Slint framework, and is designed to maintain a persistent communication channel with trusted external users that can remain continuously active. The post on Hacker News has received 22 points and generated seven comments.
summary: A new project called Flipflop creates iroh-powered persistent tunnels for file sharing. The author built it to address frustrations with LocalSend and DashBeam, using the Slint framework and aiming for always‑on trusted communication.

content:
Ancestry is promoting a 50% discount for October 2026, according to newly released coupon codes. The offer applies to the company’s family‑history memberships and DNA testing kits.

The promotion is described as a seasonal discount that combines special offers and coupon codes to help customers save on these services.

content:

content:
Groupon has announced a set of promo codes for October 2026 that provide discounts of up to 60 percent. The offer includes up to 60 percent off individual items, 40 percent off packages and a 20 percent reduction with the top Groupon coupon codes.

The coupons are promoted for savings on travel getaways, holiday gifts, spa days and event tickets.

title: Poland aims for economic growth as wages rise and living costs climb
content:
Poland is being portrayed as a nation that has risen economically since the Soviet era, with wages soaring even as the cost of living climbs, according to the final installment of a series on the country. The piece also raises questions about whether increased military spending will support or impede Poland’s growth and notes the country’s push for European Union energy resilience in response to Russian aggression.

From an observation deck atop the Varso tower in Warsaw, the city’s skyline includes the Soviet‑era Palace of Culture and Science, a building that continues to split public opinion. Some view the structure as a relic of oppression that should be removed, while others regard it as an iconic landmark and a stark reminder of history.
summary: Poles say wages have surged while the cost of living has also increased. The article also raises questions about the impact of military spending on growth and notes Poland’s push for EU energy resilience amid Russian aggression, referencing the divided views on the Soviet‑era Palace of Culture and Science.

content: A morning news bulletin was issued on October 15, 2026, presenting a roundup of the most important stories from Europe and beyond. title: Four-lane bridge linking China and North Korea opens after ten-year delay
content:
A new four‑lane bridge linking China and North Korea has opened, ending a project that was delayed for ten years.  

The opening occurs roughly one month after North Korea and Russia inaugurated a road bridge intended to strengthen their bilateral ties.
summary: A new four-lane bridge connecting China and North Korea has opened after a decade of delay. Its opening follows the opening of a road bridge between North Korea and Russia about a month earlier.
author: Euronews

title: Kaja Kallas exclusive interview as EU summit on energy, budget and Ukraine starts
content:
Kaja Kallas, identified in the report as the EU’s top diplomat, spoke exclusively to Euronews presenter Maria Tadeo as EU leaders gathered in Brussels for the opening of a crucial summit.

The summit agenda focuses on spiralling energy prices, an unfinished seven‑year EU budget and the impact of Donald Trump’s pressure on Ukraine, according to the coverage.

The broadcast also includes an interview with Abu Abughazaleh, Jordan’s Investment Minister.
summary: Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, speaks exclusively to Maria Tadeo as EU leaders arrive in Brussels for a crucial EU summit. title: Hundreds protest in Bangkok against IMF and World Bank meetings
content:
Hundreds of protesters marched through Bangkok on Thursday, 15 October, to voice opposition to the International Monetary Fund and World Bank’s annual meetings being held in the Thai capital.  

The demonstrators decried the two institutions and warned that their policies promote “destructive capitalism.”  

The rally coincided with the scheduled IMF and World Bank gatherings in Bangkok.
summary: Hundreds of protesters marched through Bangkok on Thursday, 15 October. The demonstration opposed the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings being held in the city.
author: Euronews

title: Thousands protest across Colombia against President Abelardo de la Espriella's policies
content:
Thousands of Colombians marched peacefully across the country on Wednesday, protesting against the policies of right‑wing President Abelardo de la Espriella. The demonstrations marked the opposition’s first major show of force since he took office in August.

In Bogotá, former leftist president Gustavo Petro led a rally that drew trade unionists, Indigenous groups, students, and feminist activists. The protestors gathered to voice their concerns about the new administration’s direction.
summary: Thousands of Colombians protested peacefully across the country on Wednesday against right‑wing President Abelardo de la Espriella, marking the opposition’s first major demonstrations since he took office in August. Former leftist president Gustavo Petro led a rally in Bogota that was joined by trade unionists, Indigenous groups, students and feminist activists.
author: France 24

title: EU leaders convene Thursday summit to seal €2 trillion 2028‑2034 budget by Christmas
content:
EU leaders are convening at a summit on Thursday to negotiate a deal on the European Union’s budget for 2028‑2034, which totals nearly €2 trillion. The negotiations aim to reach an agreement by Christmas.

The talks come amid deep divisions among member states over spending priorities and growing concerns that upcoming elections, especially in France, could bolster eurosceptic forces.
summary: EU leaders are heading to a Thursday summit to reach a deal on the European Union’s nearly €2 trillion budget for 2028‑2034. The talks face deep spending divisions and concerns that upcoming elections, especially in France, could boost eurosceptic forces, with a goal to finalize the budget by Christmas.
author: France 24

title: Russia strikes Izmail port and two cargo ships en route to Odesa
content:
Russia struck Ukraine’s Izmail port and hit two cargo ships traveling to Odesa, the Russian Defence Ministry said Thursday.  

A day earlier, Moscow launched additional missiles and drones at Ukrainian cities, reportedly knocking out power to hundreds of thousands of residents.  

The Defence Ministry’s statement was part of a live update on the ongoing conflict.
summary: Russia struck Ukraine's Izmail port and two cargo ships heading to Odesa, according to the Russian Defence Ministry. Earlier, Moscow launched missiles and drones that knocked out power to hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian residents.
author: France 24

title: PSG beat Manchester City 4-2 on Champions League Matchday 2
content:
Paris Saint‑Germain secured a 4‑2 win over Manchester City in a Champions League matchday 2 thriller, keeping them at the top of the group table.  

The French side dominated the first half, taking a 3‑0 advantage before the second half. Manchester City fought back, with Erling Haaland scoring twice to bring the score to 3‑2, but could not complete the comeback.  

PSG remain ahead of Barcelona in the league‑phase standings and will face the Spanish club next Tuesday.
summary: PSG defeated Manchester City 4-2 in the Champions League after leading 3-0 at halftime. The victory left PSG atop the league-phase table, ahead of Barcelona, whom they will face next Tuesday.
author: France 24

title: EU summit in Brussels to discuss China trade deficit, Ukraine and next budget
content:
EU leaders gathered in Brussels for a summit that will centre on relations with China, the situation in Ukraine and the European Union’s budget.  

The agenda includes examining measures to curb the bloc’s large trade deficit with China and seeking further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of major elections scheduled for next year.
summary: EU leaders are meeting in Brussels to examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. They also aim to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of major elections next year.
author: DW World

title: Brazil Congress approves amendment limiting work week to 40 hours
content:
Brazil’s Congress has approved a constitutional amendment that bans six‑day workweeks, limiting the legal maximum to 40 hours per week. The change could affect up to 30 million workers and would give many employees an extra day off each week.

The amendment is seen as a political win for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who has championed the measure in an effort to counter the first‑round lead of far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The vote comes just weeks before the presidential runoff.
summary: Brazil's Congress approved a constitutional amendment limiting the work week to a maximum of 40 hours, potentially affecting 30 million workers and providing a political win for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva before the runoff. Lula has strongly championed the amendment, which would give some workers an extra day off each week.
author: Guardian World

title: Argentina's Milei backs Trump, says US midterm vote crucial for West
content:
Argentina’s President Javier Milei publicly endorsed former U.S. President Donald Trump for the upcoming U.S. midterm elections, describing the vote as “crucial for the West.” While accepting an award in Washington, Milei warned that conservatives “cannot give an inch” in Latin America.

Milei’s comments linked the U.S. election to broader regional strategy, emphasizing a hard‑line stance toward left‑leaning governments in the hemisphere. The remarks were made during the award ceremony, underscoring his alignment with the U.S. president’s agenda.
summary: Milei backed Donald Trump for the U.S. midterm elections and said the vote is crucial for the West. While accepting an award in Washington, he said conservatives cannot give an inch in Latin America.

content:
Heavy rain triggered a mass pileup in Brazil’s Anhangabau tunnel, according to reports. Flooding in the area caused vehicles to become stacked inside the tunnel, leaving drivers and passengers stranded.

The incident occurred in Sao Paulo’s Anhangabau tunnel, where the floodwaters forced cars to pile up and left people trapped within the tunnel. No further details on casualties or rescue efforts were provided.

content:
Governments attending COP17 and COP31 are being urged to accelerate positive tipping points in the sectors of energy, food and finance, according to the theme “Restoring nature is key to a more resilient future.”

content:

content: G20 finance ministers and central bankers assembled in Thailand as the fallout from the Iran war intensified. content:
Israel’s upcoming election on October 27 is being closely monitored across the continent, from Morocco to South Africa.  

Analysts say the vote could serve as a test of whether Israel’s diplomatic and economic relationships with African nations can endure the repercussions of the war on Gaza.

title: Brooklyn novelty shop Art of Play says staff threatened after Kelly Clarkson complaint
content:
Brooklyn novelty shop Art of Play has become the focus of a dispute with singer Kelly Clarkson after the artist complained online about her treatment at the store over a mechanical bird.  

The shop says its employees have received threats following Clarkson’s public criticism.  

Art of Play confirmed the threats and noted the incident has placed the store at the centre of a “surreal” row with the singer.

title: Orange haze blankets Palangka Raya as nearby wildfires rage
content:
Thick orange smog enveloped the Indonesian city of Palangka Raya, prompting residents to share footage of the haze blanketing the town, according to reports. The dense orange haze descended as nearby wildfires continued to rage.

The visual documentation highlights the extent of the air pollution affecting Palangka Raya while the surrounding fires remain active.
summary: Thick orange smog covered Palangka Raya, prompting Indonesians to share footage of the haze. The smog is linked to wildfires that continue raging nearby.

title: White House defends new press secretary despite questions about bar registration
content:
The White House has defended its newly appointed press secretary after media reports raised questions about her legal credentials.  

Katie Zacharia, the new press secretary, does not appear to be registered to the legal bar in any state where she has lived.  

White House officials said the appointment remains appropriate despite the lack of bar registration.

title: Retired US generals urge Pentagon to stop livestream of Nidal Hasan execution
content:
Seventy‑two retired U.S. generals have urged the Pentagon to cancel a planned livestream of the execution of Nidal Hasan, describing the broadcast as “barbaric.”  

In a letter, the former officers warned that livestreaming the execution “will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it.”

title: West Ham defeat nine-man Lincoln 6-0 as Soucek scores twice
content:
West Ham United secured a 6-0 victory over Lincoln City at the ProAmpac Stadium, returning to winning ways in the Championship. The match was defined by early disciplinary issues for the hosts, as Tom Hamer was sent off after just three minutes and Conor McGrandles followed him off the pitch 20 minutes later, leaving Lincoln with nine men.

Konstantinos Mavropanos headed West Ham into the lead on the stroke of half-time. Tomas Soucek completed the scoring for the visitors, doubling his tally to finish the big win. Other Championship action included Portsmouth, who struck late to defeat a 10-man Sheffield United side.
summary: West Ham secured a 6-0 Championship victory against Lincoln, who were reduced to nine men after two red cards. Tomas Soucek scored twice to complete the win for the hosts.

title: Manchester City staff join government trade delegation to India
content:
A representative from Manchester City joined a government-backed trade delegation to India this week, despite the club’s recent conviction for 114 breaches of Premier League rules. The trip was organized by business secretary Jonathan Reynolds and included visits to Delhi and Mumbai.

Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig, who is the successor to Andy Burnham, led the delegation alongside other northern mayors. The group focused on promoting British trade and tourism during their stay in India.
summary: A Manchester City representative was invited on a government trade trip to India despite the club being found guilty of 114 Premier League rule breaches. Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig took the representative to Delhi and Mumbai on a delegation organized by business secretary Jonathan Reynolds.

title: CREW sues to bar Kushner from government role under Appointments Clause
content:
Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) filed a lawsuit on Wednesday challenging the legality of Jared Kushner’s position within the Trump administration. The watchdog group’s legal action specifically targets Kushner’s role in his father-in-law’s government.

The lawsuit argues that Kushner is occupying a government position and exercising government authority in violation of the Appointments Clause. CREW stated that the primary objective of the suit is to bar Kushner from holding this office.
summary: Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington filed a lawsuit on Wednesday challenging the legality of Jared Kushner's role in the Trump administration. The suit seeks to bar Kushner from occupying his government position and exercising authority in violation of the Appointments Clause.

title: Poll: 71% of Americans oppose live broadcast executions
content:
A new YouGov survey indicates that the majority of Americans oppose the public broadcasting of executions, a finding that emerges ahead of the Pentagon’s planned livestreamed execution of Nidal Hasan, the convicted Fort Hood shooter. The poll revealed that 71 percent of respondents opposed having executions broadcast live to the public.

In contrast, 18 percent of participants supported the practice, while 13 percent indicated they were unsure. The survey also noted differences in opinion along partisan lines.
summary: A YouGov poll found that 71 percent of Americans oppose having executions broadcast live to the public. This opposition exists ahead of the Pentagon’s planned livestreamed execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan.
author: The Hill

title: Vienna team finds Gas5 RNA regulates NUP98::KDM5A condensates in aggressive AML
content:
Researchers at the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna, working with the CeMM Research Center for Molecular Medicine and St. Anna Children’s Cancer Research, have created a new analytical method that identifies RNA molecules involved in cancer‑promoting cellular structures.  

Using this method, the Vienna‑based team discovered that the RNA molecule Gas5 regulates NUP98::KDM5A oncogenic condensates, which control gene activity in aggressive forms of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The findings offer a new starting point for cancer research and potential improvements in patient treatment.  

The study was published in the journal The EMBO Journal.
summary: Researchers at the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna, together with the CeMM Research Center for Molecular Medicine and St. Anna Children's Cancer Research, developed a new analytical method to identify RNA molecules involved in cancer-promoting cellular structures. Using the method they identified the RNA molecule Gas5 as an important regulator of NUP98::KDM5A oncogenic condensates that control gene activity in aggressive forms of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and the study was published in The EMBO Journal.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experts say 4,000 to 10,000 daily steps offer health benefits for weight loss
content:
Experts state that there is no single answer to how many steps are required daily for weight loss, despite the frequent repetition of the 10,000-step benchmark. While fitness trackers and smartwatches have become popular tools for monitoring activity to support health goals, specific step counts vary for individual results.

Research indicates that taking between 4,000 and 10,000 steps per day can provide health benefits, suggesting that lower activity levels may still contribute to positive outcomes.
summary: Experts state there is no single step count required for weight loss, though the 10,000-step target is commonly cited. Research indicates that taking between 4,000 and 10,000 steps per day can provide health benefits.
author: Medical Xpress

title: One-third of global food lost or wasted as policy focuses on production
content: Globally, approximately one-third of food produced for human consumption is estimated to be lost or wasted. While agricultural policy in the Global South has primarily focused on increasing production to address climate change and resource constraints, the issue of postharvest losses remains a significant challenge.
summary: Globally, about one-third of food produced for human consumption is estimated to be lost or wasted. Policy responses in the Global South have focused on increasing production rather than addressing postharvest losses.

content: Publishing scientific articles relies on more than just knowledge of academic writing conventions, as it also depends on access to networks that support the research and publication process. These academic networks provide opportunities for researchers to exchange knowledge, receive feedback, and develop collaborations that strengthen both their research and careers. For researchers in vulnerable situations, such connections are particularly crucial.
summary: Publishing scientific articles depends on access to networks that support research and career development. These connections are crucial for researchers in vulnerable situations who exchange knowledge and develop collaborations.
